title: The Future of Primary Care

reader_summary.headline: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast. Primary care was meant to be the front door to the health care system. We need a new operating system for primary care, one with a different, deeper understanding of the patient, the context of their world around them.

key_points.text: Primary care was meant to be the front door to the health care system.
key_points.evidence_quote: Primary care was meant to be the front door to the health care system, but in some ways it was never set up for success to begin with.

key_points.text: We need a new operating system for primary care, one with a different, deeper understanding of the patient.
key_points.evidence_quote: We need a new operating system for primary care, one with a different, deeper understanding of the patient, the context of their world around them, and the data and processes we have in place to figure out who sees a doctor and when to use the whole healthcare system most efficiently.

key_points.text: In this episode of the A16C podcast, we talk about what the primary care of the future should actually look like.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode of the A16C podcast, we talk about what the primary care of the future should actually look like.

key_points.text: Joining us for the conversation, our A16Z general partner, Julie Yu, physician-entrepreneur, Dr.
key_points.evidence_quote: Joining us for the conversation, our A16Z general partner, Julie Yu, physician-entrepreneur, Dr.

thesis: The episode argues that primary care must evolve from a reactive model focused on diagnosing illness to a proactive system centered on continuous health monitoring and risk stratification. It posits that the future of primary care requires an automated data collection layer to efficiently triage patients, ensuring that scarce doctor time is reserved for those requiring intervention while leveraging support staff and community health workers to manage low-acuity needs.
